Chapter 12: The Forty Days and Ascension—Preparing for What Comes Next.
So, imagine this... After the shock and sheer wonder of the resurrection, there’s this quiet season of preparation. For forty days, Jesus stays close to His friends—teaching, comforting, and guiding them. The world outside? Still the same. Still uncertain, still full of challenges. But inside that small circle of disciples, hope was starting to flicker back to life.
Jesus talked about forgiveness. About the incredible power of the Spirit. And about a mission that would reach far beyond the familiar hills of Galilee. They shared meals, they asked tough questions, and He never shied away from their doubts. It became obvious—the story wasn’t over. In fact, it was about to begin again, just in a whole new way.
Then, one morning on a hillside just outside Jerusalem, Jesus gathered them all for one last time. He blessed them, promised they’d never be alone, and then—right in front of their eyes—He was taken from their sight. The sky seemed to open up, and this extraordinary promise of return hung in the air.
For those left behind, the days that followed were a mix of longing and newfound purpose. They clung to His words, leaned on each other, and waited for the Spirit He’d promised. The ascension wasn’t just a farewell—it was a commissioning. A call to take the message of hope, love, and redemption out into the world.
You know, most people don’t realize just how much courage it takes to step into the unknown. The disciples, who’d once been so afraid and uncertain, found new strength in the memory of Jesus’ presence—and the assurance that He was still caring for them.
The story of those forty days and the ascension? It’s a powerful reminder that every ending is also a new beginning. And even when the path ahead feels unclear, the work of love keeps going.
